passages.note: House third-reading roll call 305 on SB 101; Clere is listed under Nay.

passages.provision_quote: A governmental entity may substantially burden a person's exercise of religion only if the governmental entity demonstrates that application of the burden to the person: (1) is in furtherance of a compelling governmental interest; and (2) is the least restrictive means of furthering that compelling governmental interest.
passages.note: Enrolled act text prints the strict-scrutiny exemption standard the chamber voted on; it does not itself name any voter.

rows.reasoning: Rep. Clere voted Nay in House Roll Call 305 on final passage of SB 101 (2015), a single-subject Religious Freedom Restoration Act providing that a governmental entity may substantially burden a person's exercise of religion only if it demonstrates a compelling governmental interest pursued by the least restrictive means. A No vote on this exemption regime shows only that he opposed extending faith-based exemptions this far; it does not establish which remaining position he holds, whether prohibiting religious exemptions from anti-discrimination law, protecting religious freedom while preserving anti-discrimination protections in employment and housing, or balancing religious practice with equal treatment.
needs_source: Rep. Clere's own statement or floor explanation of his Nay vote on SB 101 (2015), if any exists, to show which specific balance between religious freedom and anti-discrimination protection he supports.
